title: Cross-addon native buffer interoperability
objective: Determine and regression-test whether separately compiled native kernels can share IntegerBuffer, Int64Buffer, and Float64Buffer values safely; implement a narrow lifetime-safe compiler/runtime fix only if justified, otherwise document the unified-compilation boundary

oracles: JavaScript typed-array semantics and isolated native-addon differential execution

handoff.summary: Confirmed that matching IntegerBuffer, Int64Buffer, and Float64Buffer values use host-owned typed-array storage and cross independently compiled native addons synchronously without copies. The reported candidate-to-bridge failure is a prep_state ABI mismatch: the candidate publishes IntegerBuffer while the bridge declares Int64Buffer. Generated wrappers now reject that mismatch explicitly, with a focused two-addon native regression covering in-place cross-addon mutation and unchanged backing storage.
risks: The producer/bridge application sources still need to agree on prep_state's declared type; this compiler change diagnoses rather than converts the mismatch.
The full unit tier reached its final batch before an unrelated browser test failed because dist/wasi-runtime.mjs returned 404.
next_steps: Align prep_state as IntegerBuffer across the live prepared-H1 producer and bridge, then rerun that end-to-end worker.
